notes: There is NO stock/inventory column. If asked about stock, answer that stock data is unavailable.
Prefer JOINs when product names, brand names, category names, or issue names are needed.
customer_queries stores RetailAsk owner chat history with the bot — not customer product feedback.
customer_feedback stores customer sentiment, issues, and returns about products.
Return information is on customer_feedback.is_return and customer_feedback.return_reason (no separate returns table).

Business semantics — high sales / high-selling: measure each product's total units sold as SUM(sales.quantity). Treat a product as high-selling when that total is greater than or equal to the median of per-product SUM(sales.quantity) values across products that have sales. Compute that median dynamically in MySQL 8 using window functions (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_quantity) and COUNT(*) OVER (), then AVG of middle row(s) with rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)). Do NOT use LIMIT/OFFSET expressions with nested SELECT arithmetic to compute the median (invalid in MySQL). Do NOT invent absolute thresholds such as SUM(quantity) > 100. Do NOT hardcode a fixed median number from memory.

Business semantics — quality issues: a product has a quality issue when it has customer_feedback linked to an Issue (customer_feedback.issue_id IS NOT NULL and/or JOIN issues). Quality issues are NOT the same as returns. Do NOT filter on customer_feedback.is_return when the question asks about quality issues unless the question also explicitly mentions returns.
Business semantics — returns: use customer_feedback.is_return = 1 only when the user's question explicitly refers to returns/returned/refunds.
Business semantics — do not invent feedback-count thresholds such as COUNT(feedback_id) > 5 (or similar) unless the user explicitly asks for a count or numeric threshold.

tables.purpose: Product catalog for the retail store. Each row is a sellable item with price and links to brand and category.

columns.name: product_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a product.

columns.name: product_name
columns.meaning: Human-readable product name (e.g. Laptop, Mouse).

columns.name: price
columns.meaning: Unit list price of the product.

columns.name: brand_id
columns.meaning: Foreign key to brands.brand_id — which brand owns this product.

columns.name: category_id
columns.meaning: Foreign key to categories.category_id — product category.

example_questions: Which products are priced above $200?
List all products with their brand and category.
What is the price of the Laptop?

tables.purpose: Sales / transaction line items. Each row records quantity and revenue for one product on a sale date. Use for revenue totals, top-selling products, sales trends, and high-sales analysis via SUM(quantity) compared to the dynamic median of per-product totals.

columns.name: sale_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a sale row.

columns.name: product_id
columns.meaning: Foreign key to products.product_id — which product was sold.

columns.name: sale_date
columns.meaning: Date the sale occurred.

columns.name: quantity
columns.meaning: Number of units sold in this sale.

columns.name: total_price
columns.meaning: Total revenue for this sale line (quantity × price).

example_questions: Which products have the highest sales?
Which products have high sales?
What were total sales this month?
What is the average order value?
Which brand generates the most sales revenue?
Which category has the most sales?

tables.purpose: Brand lookup table. Use when questions ask about brands, brand performance, or brand-level sales.

columns.name: brand_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a brand.

columns.name: brand_name
columns.meaning: Brand display name (e.g. TechNova, SoundMax).

example_questions: Which brands generate the most sales?
List all brands in the catalog.
How many products does each brand have?

tables.purpose: Product category lookup table. Use for category revenue, category rankings, and grouping products by category.

columns.name: category_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a category.

columns.name: category_name
columns.meaning: Category display name (e.g. Computers, Audio, Furniture).

example_questions: Which category has the most sales?
Which category has the highest revenue?
How many products are in each category?

tables.purpose: Issue type lookup for customer feedback (quality problems, delivery, compatibility, etc.). Join from customer_feedback.issue_id when analyzing quality issues or issue types. Having an issue link means a quality/classified issue — not a return flag.

columns.name: issue_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying an issue type.

columns.name: issue_name
columns.meaning: Issue label such as Defective product, Battery life, Durability.

example_questions: Which products have quality issues?
Which products have high sales and quality issues?
What are the most common issue types?
Which issue is linked to the most returns?

tables.purpose: Customer product feedback for retail-owner analytics. Includes sentiment (positive/negative/neutral), optional issue link (quality/classified issues via issue_id), and separate return flags (is_return). Quality issues use issue_id/JOIN issues; returns use is_return only when asked. NOT the same as customer_queries chat history.

columns.name: feedback_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a feedback row.

columns.name: product_id
columns.meaning: Foreign key to products.product_id — product the feedback is about.

columns.name: issue_id
columns.meaning: Optional foreign key to issues.issue_id — classified quality/issue type. Non-NULL means this feedback is linked to a quality issue. Not equivalent to is_return.

columns.name: feedback_text
columns.meaning: Free-text customer feedback comment.

columns.name: sentiment
columns.meaning: Sentiment label for the feedback.

columns.name: is_return
columns.meaning: Boolean flag: 1 if this feedback is associated with a return, else 0. Use only for return questions — not a proxy for quality issues.

columns.name: return_reason
columns.meaning: Optional reason when is_return is true.

columns.name: feedback_date
columns.meaning: When the feedback was recorded.

example_questions: Which products have negative feedback and returns?
Which products have quality issues?
Which products have high sales and quality issues?
Show products with many returns.
What is the sentiment breakdown by product?

tables.purpose: RetailAsk owner chat history: natural-language questions asked to the bot and the bot responses. Use only for summarizing past owner queries — not for product feedback, sentiment, or returns.

columns.name: query_id
columns.meaning: Primary key uniquely identifying a chat log row.

columns.name: query_text
columns.meaning: Owner question typed into RetailAsk.

columns.name: response
columns.meaning: Bot answer that was returned.

columns.name: query_date
columns.meaning: When the chat exchange was saved.

example_questions: Summarize recent owner questions to the bot.
What have users been asking RetailAsk lately?
Show recent customer_queries chat history.
